why_this_works: The vodka dissolves flavor compounds in the tomato paste that are alcohol-soluble but not water- or fat-soluble, unlocking a fuller tomato taste you can't get otherwise. Browning the sausage hard before building the sauce creates a fond that deglazes into the vodka, adding meaty depth. The heavy cream emulsifies with the tomato paste to create a stable, silky sauce that clings to penne.
notes: Use double-concentrated tomato paste (Mutti or DeLallo). Don't sub the heavy cream for milk or half-and-half — it'll curdle. Buy bulk Italian sausage or remove from casings.

steps: Boil a generously salted pot of water and cook the penne al dente according to package directions.
Meanwhile, add butter, sausage meat, and onions to a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook 7-10 minutes until nicely browned, breaking the sausage up as you go. Drain excess fat.
Stir in the garlic and vodka. Let the sauce bubble for about 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomato paste and cream until you have a smooth mixture.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Let the sauce warm through and thicken to your liking.
Season with salt and pepper. Stir in fresh basil if using. Toss with drained pasta, thinning with a splash of pasta water if needed. Serve with freshly grated parmesan.
